data.hypothesis: The earlier full-cooperative candidate passed correctness but measured 0.762 ms versus the 46.244 μs baseline. This experiment tests whether limiting the cooperative grid to at most four resident CTAs per SM reduces grid-barrier and partial-handling costs, while retaining the ordinary path below 1<<20 to avoid cooperative setup costs on smaller inputs. The reduced grid may lower throughput; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Cooperative launch correctness alone does not establish that it is a good path for this reduction; compare the full run cost and test a contrasting residency-safe grid size.
memory_lessons.claim: The earlier cooperative candidate was correct on all 10 reported cases but measured 0.7616 ms mean, compared with the baseline's 46.244 μs. The result supports testing a different grid-size policy without attributing the slowdown to a specific cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this candidate, including per-call device, property, occupancy, and cooperative-launch costs; check correctness and timing across all valid sizes.

data.notes: The earlier cooperative candidate was validated correct but slower than baseline; its preceding development attempt had a build failure. This proposal contrasts its maximum-occupancy grid with a four-CTA-per-SM cap and routes smaller inputs through the ordinary reduction. No unsupported-runtime result was provided. The controller must validate and measure this source; no new performance or correctness claim is made.
transformations: Replace the previous maximum-occupancy cooperative grid with a grid capped at four occupancy-verified CTAs per SM, using grid-stride input processing and a cooperative grid barrier before CTA 0 reduces the fully written partials.
Use the cooperative path only for n >= 1<<20; preserve a conventional multi-kernel fallback when it is smaller, unavailable, or rejected at launch.
Perform reduction stages with unsigned 32-bit additions to avoid signed-overflow intermediate arithmetic, and write zero for n <= 0.
